questions.q: A hardware or software barrier that filters traffic between your network and the Internet by rules is a —
questions.solution: **Firewall** = the rule-based doorman of a network.

questions.q: The Find and Replace dialog in MS Word opens directly on the Replace tab with:
questions.solution: Ctrl+H opens Replace. Ctrl+F opens the Navigation (find) pane, Ctrl+G opens Go To, and Ctrl+R right-aligns text.
questions.shortcut: H = cHange/replace in Word (but History in a browser).

questions.q: Which address CHANGES when a laptop moves from your home network to office Wi-Fi?
questions.solution: The **IP is logical and network-dependent**; the MAC stays burnt into the card forever.

questions.q: Hacking (computer-related offences) is punished under which section of the IT Act?
questions.solution: **Sec 66** = computer-related offences — the 'hacking' section with dishonest intent.

questions.q:
Choose the sentence that best completes the paragraph.

Film tickets in the multiplexes now cost a family of four more than a full month of a streaming subscription, and the popcorn is extra.
options: When an outing costs a month of home viewing, the sofa wins.
Cinemas should screen more regional films.
OTT platforms raise prices every year too.
questions.solution: The paragraph sets up the price comparison; option 1 lands the implied conclusion. Option 3 argues back instead of completing; the rest drift.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He has been working in this office ___ five years.
questions.solution: A length of time takes **for**; since needs a starting point (since 2021).

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To face the music
options: to accept the unpleasant results of one's own actions
questions.solution: *Face the music* = to accept criticism or punishment for what one has done. The concert and loud-music options are literal; 'run away from punishment' is the opposite.
questions.shortcut: Kill the two music options; the opposite is the last trap.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Mother often says, "Honesty is the best policy."
options: Mother often says that honesty was the best policy.
Mother often said that honesty is the best policy.
Mother often says that honesty is the better policy.
Mother often says that honesty is the best policy.
questions.solution: Present frame **says** keeps the quote in the present: **is the best policy** — doubly safe because the sentence is also a universal truth. 'Was the best policy' backshifts twice wrongly; 'often said' moves the reporting verb; 'the better policy' corrupts the superlative.
questions.shortcut: Present frame + universal truth = nothing shifts.

questions.q: Fossils of plants and animals are found only in which type of rock?
questions.solution: Only **sedimentary rocks** form in layers at the surface, where living remains can be buried; heat and pressure in other rocks destroy them.

questions.q:
Consider the statements:
1. The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878.
2. The Delhi Durbar of 1877 proclaimed Victoria 'Empress of India'.
3. The Arms Act of Lytton's time disarmed Indians.
Which are correct?
questions.solution: All three belong to **Lytton's** tenure (1876–80): the press gag (1878), the 1877 Durbar, and the Arms Act.
questions.shortcut: Lytton's trio: press gag, Arms Act, Durbar.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution is called its '**heart and soul**' by Dr B.R. Ambedkar?
questions.solution: **Article 32** (right to constitutional remedies) — Ambedkar's phrase, because without the writ power the other rights would be declarations only.

questions.q: The President of India is elected by —
options: An electoral college of elected MPs and elected MLAs
questions.solution: The electoral college has **elected MPs**, **elected MLAs of the states**, and (since the 70th Amendment) elected MLAs of **Delhi and Puducherry**. Voting is by proportional representation, single transferable vote.
questions.shortcut: Elected MPs + elected MLAs (states, Delhi, Puducherry).

questions.q: The hypotenuse of a right triangle is $13$ cm and one leg is $5$ cm. Its area is:
questions.solution:
Other leg $= \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12$ cm (5-12-13).

$K = \frac12 \times 5 \times 12 = 30$ sq cm.
questions.shortcut: Missing leg 12 → $30$ sq cm. Trap: $32.5$ ($\frac12 \times 5 \times 13$ used the hypotenuse).

questions.q: 4 different toys are to be distributed among 3 children. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.solution: Each toy has 3 choices of child: $3^4 = 81$.

questions.q: The length and breadth of a rectangle are 24 cm and 18 cm. Its perimeter is:
questions.shortcut: $2\times(24+18)=84$. Trap: 432 is the area; 42 forgot to double.

questions.q: A and B together can do a work in 8 days, B and C in 12 days, and A and C in 16 days. All three together will complete it in:
questions.shortcut: Pairwise rates add to 2× the trio rate ⇒ 96/13 days.

questions.q: If the signs **+ and ÷ are interchanged**, what is the value of **63 + 9 ÷ 14 − 3 × 2**?
questions.solution: After the swap: **63 ÷ 9 + 14 − 3 × 2**. 63 ÷ 9 = 7 and 3 × 2 = 6. Then 7 + 14 − 6 = **15**. (Left to right gives 36.)
questions.shortcut: Swap both signs everywhere, then BODMAS.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**Gold, Silver, Platinum, Brass**
questions.solution: Gold, silver and platinum are **pure metals (elements)**. Brass is an **alloy** - a mixture of copper and zinc → **Brass**.

questions.q: In a certain code language, **'go to school' = '5 7 9'**, **'to the park' = '7 2 4'** and **'school bus' = '9 8'**. What is the code for **'bus go'**?
questions.solution: 'to' is common to sentences 1–2 → to = 7. 'school' is common to 1–3 → school = 9. Sentence 3 leaves bus = 8; sentence 1 leaves go = 5. 'Bus go' = **8 5**.

questions.q:
In each triangle the corners are (left, right, top) and a number sits in the centre:

**(2, 3, 4) → 20**

**(1, 5, 3) → 18**

**(4, 2, 5) → ?**
questions.solution: Product of corners fails (24 ≠ 20), sum fails (9). Rule: centre = (left + right) × top: (2 + 3) × 4 = 20 ✓, (1 + 5) × 3 = 18 ✓. So (4 + 2) × 5 = **30**. (40 is the product of all three corners.)
questions.shortcut: Centre just below the corner product → try (x + y) × z.
